title: PH envoy Babe Romualdez stresses no data centers eyed in New Clark City
summary: Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel "Babe" Romualdez reiterated on Thursday that no data centers will be built under the US-led Pax Silica initiative in Clark, noting that they are…

blocks.text: Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel "Babe" Romualdez reiterated on Thursday that no data centers will be built under the US-led Pax Silica initiative in Clark, noting that they are now calling the projects as a "manufacturing hub" rather than "Pax Silica."
“Wala naman pinag-uusapan na data center na igaganap diyan sa Pax Silica eh. So ‘yung Pax Silica is a manufacturing hub for critical [minerals],” Romualdez said on Super Radyo dzBB.
(There has never been any discussion about setting up a data center under Pax Silica. Instead, Pax Silica is a manufacturing hub for critical minerals.)
“Actually we’re not even calling it Pax Silica, it's more of a development, manufacturing hub that will have not only US companies, but other companies rin,” he added.

The envoy said critical minerals like nickel, which the Philippines typically exports raw and at low prices to China, can now be processed and diversified inside the hub, giving them significantly higher market value.
Citing his discussions with Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Romualdez said data centers were never part of the Pax Silica plans.

“Eh hindi naman natin pwedeng ilagay [ang data centers] sa Clark dahil that is already an economic zone that is already we’re putting manufacturing potentials there and other aspects of our economy is going to be located in the Clark Economic Zone,” Romualdez said.
(We cannot put data centers in Clark because that is already an economic zone where we are placing manufacturing facilities and other key sectors of our economy.)
“So wala sa usapan yang mga ganiyan na data centers (Data centers are really not part of the plan),” he added.
The Pax Silica initiative drew protests from various groups across the country ahead of US President Donald Trump’s state visit to the Philippines earlier this week.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton had previously clarified that no signing of the Pax Silica agreement was scheduled during Trump’s visit.
The Pax Silica initiative is a US-led effort to build a network of allied supply chains for critical technologies and minerals, which the Philippines will host in New Clark City in Tarlac.

Government officials have clarified that there will be no data centers included in the Pax Silica initiative, as its main objective is to process the country’s minerals and manufacture high-tech components for semiconductors and artificial intelligence. —NB, GMA News
